item.content:encoded:
South Korea's Lee says hopes reopening talks with North Korea could lead to lasting peace South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Thursday he hoped a reopening of dialogue with North Korea would lead to discussions on ending the Korean War and establishing a lasting peace, as he addressed Asia-Pacific leaders in China. Reuters | Updated: 19-11-2026 12:55 IST | Created: 19-11-2026 12:55 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Thursday he hoped a reopening of dialogue with North Korea would lead to discussions on ending the Korean War and establishing a lasting peace, as he addressed Asia-Pacific leaders in China. Speaking at a session of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, Lee said peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula were essential to shared regional prosperity and urged members to take an active interest and cooperate, according to the Korean presidential office. His statement came ahead of a trilateral summit between the leaders of Russia, China and the United States at APEC, with some analysts saying North Korea's nuclear weapons and sanctions on Pyongyang could be among the issues discussed. South Korea's National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac told a briefing on Wednesday that Chinese President Xi Jinping told Lee at talks on the sidelines of the summit that Beijing would play a constructive role to realise peace on the Korean Peninsula. Lee also held a meeting with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Thursday at the summit, where they agreed to cooperate on building stable and mutually beneficial energy supply chains, according to Lee's office.

item.content:encoded:
Taiwan reports two Russian military aircraft nearby, second time this week Taiwan's defence ministry said that two Russian military Tu-95 aircraft flew to the island's east on Thursday after approaching from the south, the second time this week it has reported seeing such activity. Reuters | Updated: 19-11-2026 12:46 IST | Created: 19-11-2026 12:46 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Taiwan's defence ministry said that two Russian military Tu-95 aircraft flew to the island's east on Thursday after approaching from the south, the second time this week it has reported seeing such activity. The flights have come as Russian President Vladimir Putin is in China's Shenzhen for the APEC summit, where he will also hold a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump. The ministry said the two Tu-95s, known by NATO as "Bears", entered Taiwan's Air Defence Identification Zone, then exited airspace around Taiwan to the island's northeast, off the port city of Keelung. The ministry published a picture of one of the aircraft it said was taken from a Taiwanese F-16 fighter. Taiwan's armed forces used joint intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance means to monitor the full course of the activity and "responded appropriately", the ministry said in a short statement. Taiwan said on Tuesday two Russian military aircraft had flown in a southerly direction down its east coast. Japan also reported the same activity that day and published a map showing the aircraft flying down Taiwan's east coast. An ageing Cold War-era design, some Tu-95 can carry nuclear weapons but others of that type are used for long-range surveillance and reconnaissance. Russia's defence ministry has not responded to requests for comment. Earlier on Thursday, Taiwan's envoy to the APEC summit Stan Shih, the founder of computer maker Acer, briefly shook hands with Putin at the start of the summit. Major semiconductor producer Taiwan has joined Western countries in placing wide economic sanctions on Russia since it invaded Ukraine in 2022. China's military operates around Taiwan on a daily basis. China views Taiwan as its own territory, a position Russia has repeatedly backed. Taiwan's government rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims, saying only the island's people can decide their future.

item.title: Ukraine strikes Crimean Bridge for third time in a week ahead of US-China-Russia summit
item.description: Ukraine struck the bridge linking Russia and Crimea for the third time in a week, forcing a suspension of train services across it, Russian authorities said, hours before President Vladimir Putin was ...
item.content:encoded:
Ukraine strikes Crimean Bridge for third time in a week ahead of US-China-Russia summit Ukraine struck the bridge linking Russia and Crimea for the third time in a week, forcing a suspension of train services across it, Russian authorities said, hours before President Vladimir Putin was due to meet the leaders of China and the US. Reuters | Updated: 19-11-2026 12:43 IST | Created: 19-11-2026 12:43 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Ukraine struck the bridge linking Russia and Crimea for the third time in a week, forcing a suspension of train services across it, Russian authorities said, hours before President Vladimir Putin was due to meet the leaders of China and the US. The timing and impact of Ukraine's attacks on the bridge, the longest in Europe and a symbol of Putin's Russia, are awkward for the Kremlin chief as he prepares to participate in what Moscow has cast as a historic trilateral summit with US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping later on Thursday. Moscow hopes the meeting will send a signal to allies and foes that it - and not the European Union and Britain - is part of an emerging new multilateral world order. In a statement on Thursday, Russia's transport ministry said nobody had been hurt in the Ukrainian attack on the Black Sea peninsula, which Moscow annexed from Ukraine in 2014, and that specialists were assessing damage to the bridge. "As a result of a nighttime drone attack, train services on the railway section of the Crimean Bridge have been temporarily suspended," the ministry said in a statement on Telegram. Sergei Aksyonov, Crimea's Russian-installed governor, confirmed the attack earlier on Thursday. The 19-kilometre (12-mile) bridge is a flagship project which Putin inaugurated in 2018 and is a symbol of Russia's attachment to the peninsula, which is also the home of its Black Sea Fleet. On Tuesday, Ukrainian drones and missiles destroyed the central road section of the bridge, forcing its main road arch to crumble into the sea while leaving a yawning gap, according to videos and images verified by Reuters. This week's first attack, on Monday, caused more minor damage, but gave Ukrainian forces a chance to see how Russian air defences would react.

item.title: Athletics-World marathon champion Jepchirchir banned for three years over EPO use
item.description: Kenya's world marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has been banned for three years for the use of blood booster EPO, the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) said on Thursday, adding that she admitted to ...
item.content:encoded:
Athletics-World marathon champion Jepchirchir banned for three years over EPO use Kenya's world marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has been banned for three years for the use of blood booster EPO, the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) said on Thursday, adding that she admitted to breaching anti-doping rules. Reuters | Updated: 19-11-2026 12:43 IST | Created: 19-11-2026 12:43 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Kenya's world marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has been banned for three years for the use of blood booster EPO, the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) said on Thursday, adding that she admitted to breaching anti-doping rules. One of the most decorated women in the sport, the 33-year-old has won gold at the Tokyo Games in 2021 and claimed major marathon victories in New York (2021), Boston (2022), London (2024) and Sydney. The breaches related to the "presence of a prohibited substance or its metabolites or markers in an athlete's sample" and the "use or attempted use by an athlete of a prohibited substance or a prohibited method", the AIU said. Jepchirchir was given a provisional suspension last month, after testing positive for the banned substance in a sample taken before her Sydney Marathon victory in August. The AIU said the sample returned an adverse analytical finding (AAF) on September 17. "In an interview on that same date, the athlete denied using EPO and said she had no knowledge of how the AAF had occurred," the AIU added. "Despite her explanations in the interview, the former world record-holder in the half-marathon subsequently signed an admission of anti-doping rule violations and acceptance of consequences form," it added. In the form, she accepted disqualification of all her competitive results since 17 July 2026, including her victory in the Sydney Marathon, it said. On Thursday, Sydney marathon authorities said Irine Cheptai would be crowned the 2026 women's champion after Jepchirchir's disqualification.
